evals.prompt: I'm working on the Ala 'news' Go service (it's built on our alaa-go-chi kit, chi router, pgx). Please implement the POST /api/v1/news endpoint end to end as Go source files: the route registration, the HTTP handler, the CreateNews use case, and the ports it needs. Business rules: the caller must hold the permission news_user_can_send_to_his_shobe and a fresh TOTP step-up for purpose news.insert; the request body has title (required), text (required), and an audience object with a nullable shobe_id and a user_ids list; creating a published news item must also record an audit entry and emit a notification.command.news.broadcast.v1 command. Write idiomatic production-quality Go. Put the files under outputs/ as handler.go, usecase.go, ports.go, routes.go.
evals.expected_output: States the active kit scope phase and names the freeze document before writing consumer code. Route declared with explicit trusted posture + permission + TOTP middleware; handler uses kit binder/responder (no hand-rolled JSON errors); use case receives a typed trust context (never *http.Request); broadcast command written as an outbox row in the same transaction as the news insert + audit row; typed errkit domain errors.

evals.prompt: In our Ala news Go service (alaa-go-chi kit based), I need a background 'read receipt flusher': read receipts get buffered in memory when users open a news item, and a background worker flushes them to Postgres in batches — every 2 seconds or every 500 buffered rows, whichever comes first. The table is news_read_receipts(news_id, user_id, first_read_at, last_read_at, read_count) with primary key (news_id, user_id); a re-read should bump last_read_at and read_count. It must shut down cleanly when the service stops. Write flusher.go (the worker), the SQL it executes, and how it's constructed/configured. Put files under outputs/.
evals.expected_output: States the active kit scope phase and names the freeze document before writing consumer code. Worker owns its goroutine lifecycle (context cancellation, ticker, final drain on shutdown) and participates in runkit's shutdown phases; SQL is an ON CONFLICT upsert (idempotent); flush interval/batch size injected via constructor from boot-time config (no os.Getenv in the worker); failures counted in a bounded metric and logged, not swallowed.

evals.prompt: For our Ala platform (Go services on the alaa-go-chi kit, RabbitMQ between services): define the Go message structs for the notification.command.news.broadcast.v1 command and show how the news service emits it when a news item is published. The payload carries: project_id (our canonical public project id), news_public_id, title, summary (nullable), public_url, action_btns (list of {text, url, copy_text}), force_channels (list of channel names), visibility, and an audience object with six nullable location pins (ostan_id, shahrestan_id, bakhsh_id, shahr_id, shobe_id, school_id) plus a user_ids list. The consumer on the other side is case-sensitive about JSON keys. Write command.go (structs) and emit.go (how the publish happens from the publish-news flow). Put files under outputs/.
evals.expected_output: States the active kit scope phase and names the freeze document before writing consumer code. Every struct field at every nesting level has an explicit snake_case json tag; envelope carries message_id/message_type/idempotency_key/correlation_id and trace context; project_id is a UUIDv7 string (not an int); emission writes an outbox row inside the same DB transaction as the news status change rather than publishing directly to the broker.

evals.prompt: Ala news service (alaa-go-chi kit). Add a rule to the PublishNews use case: a news item whose visibility is 'public' may only be published by a caller holding news_user_can_send_public; anything else must be rejected. Also make the publish path safe to replay — our relay sometimes redelivers the publish command. Just the implementation please, keep it tight. Put files under outputs/.
evals.expected_output: Writes tests even though the prompt asked only for implementation, because P12 makes a behavior change start with a failing test: a table-driven use-case test against fake ports asserting the errkit code for the denied case, and a run-twice test proving the replayed publish produces one state change, one outbox row, and no error. Does not fake the boundary under test. Names the tier each test belongs to (fakes at ports vs real Postgres for the ON CONFLICT/idempotency SQL) and does not claim contracttest coverage it did not run.

evals.prompt: Ala notification service work (alaa-go-chi kit). We're adding SMS fan-out through Mediana. Write the sender adapter: it should batch recipients into Mediana's bulk endpoint using their maximum batch size, and it needs each recipient's mobile number — those live in the auth service's users table, ostan_id column tells you the province. Put files under outputs/.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to invent Mediana's maximum batch size: marks it NEEDS_MEDIANA_CONFIRMATION or [gap] in the code and in the summary, makes it a configurable value with no invented default, and says what confirmation is needed. Refuses the reach-in into the auth service's users table: recipients arrive via the owning contract (the user projection command feeding a local projection, or the owning API), never a cross-service SQL query. Notes that Mediana offers no provider idempotency key, so only a queued delivery may dispatch, and routes retry/backoff policy to alaa-reliability-sla rather than inventing one.

evals.prompt: Ala news service (alaa-go-chi kit). The read-receipt buffer can lose the last couple of seconds of receipts if a pod is killed — that's fine for our use case, receipts aren't money. Drop the drain logic from the flusher so shutdown is faster, and ship it.
evals.expected_output: Does not accept the loss on the requester's say-so alone and does not remove the drain. Names the three conditions accepted loss requires: the service's own design record, cited by path, stating the maximum records and maximum time window that may be lost; a test proving the buffer is empty after the flush phase completes on graceful shutdown; a counter metric on dropped records with an alert. States which of the three are missing and asks the smallest resolving question. Explains that removing the drain also removes the only bounded-loss guarantee, and that runkit's flush phase already bounds shutdown time.

evals.prompt: Ala news service (alaa-go-chi kit). Two small things: (1) add a trace_id field to the top level of every error response so our frontend can show it, and (2) write us a little middleware that stamps X-Request-Id on responses — I couldn't find one, so just add it in internal/transport/http/middleware.
evals.expected_output: Writes no service code for either item. Identifies both surfaces as kit-owned — the canonical error envelope belongs to errkit and correlation middleware to httpkit's fixed chain — and states that a local implementation is the dual-behavior bug P1 exists to prevent. Directs the change to one timestamped change request in the kit repository's docs/change-requests/ through alaa-go-chi-development, notes the only sanctioned interim form is a thin KIT-WRAP with the request already filed and a maximum life of two kit releases, and reports the active KIT_FIRST_STABILIZATION phase. Verifies the second item against the kit's correlation surface before agreeing it is missing, rather than accepting 'I couldn't find one'.
